model.name: Feature is MISSING its type-index link folder — Features must resolve THROUGH the index like the other 18 types, never a corpus scan (structural regression, not performance)
model.description: STRUCTURAL DEFECT (Tron 2026-08-17): scenario/sprints.md/ holds a TYPE-INDEX LINK FOLDER (ln reference links) for 18 unit types — bug/changerequest/class/currentsprint/device/file/implementation/message/method/requirement/room/skill/sprint/task/test/tracelink/usecase/user — and **feature is the ONE missing**. That is WHY bootstrapSeed walks all ~5677 units: Features have no index to resolve through, so someone wrote a corpus scan instead. This is a MISSING TYPE-INDEX (wrong shape), NOT a performance problem: measured boot is ~1.3s and a full 5680-unit scan is 0.1s, so speed was never the point. FIX: restore feature's type-index folder (same ln-link convention as the other 18, invent NO new mechanism); Features resolve THROUGH it; DELETE the walk-all-units path because it is the WRONG SHAPE. Still-real hygiene retained: boot read-mostly (seed-if-absent lazily) + non-atomic Feature write -> temp+rename. ★ AUDIT (measured): feature is NOT the only gap — 11 types-in-use lack a folder (see AC-audit).
model.tronQuote: > Tron (2026-08-17): "thats the reason for having a link folder of type features with only the references ln links... like on task, class, and all the other scenario-units... when did you lose that!!!"

discoverySource.note: campaignScope=OUTSIDE, ranked ABOVE other deferred items = a latent outage that worsens daily with no code change. Capture-only, do-NOT-execute-tonight; PO schedules. Architect designed the shape (ACs are the ruling).

model.crossRefNote: Boot-health family with R40.36 (b8e5411a, scratch boot-smoke GATE — detects a boot failure). R40.39 is the boot-SHAPE FIX (corpus-independence — removes the cause R40.36 would catch). The 8-min outage + 45s hang are the same bad-boot-shape R40.36 gates and R40.39 eliminates.
model.campaignScope: OUTSIDE-S30++-finish-campaign-count, PRIORITY RESTORED (structural regression = a missing type-index, NOT hygiene, NOT performance). Corrected twice 2026-08-17 (not-slow refutation -> then Tron structural re-frame): the missing feature index is the real defect behind the corpus walk.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `feature` gets its TYPE-INDEX LINK FOLDER at scenario/sprints.md/feature/ — ln reference links to the Feature units, EXACTLY like the other 18 type folders (task, class, requirement, ...). Same convention; invent NO new mechanism. This restores what was lost.

Features resolve THROUGH the feature type-index (ln-link folder), NEVER a corpus scan. DELETE the bootstrapSeed walk-all-units path because it is the WRONG SHAPE (a type with no index got a corpus scan), NOT because it is slow.

A GATE FAILS if ANY unit type is resolved by a corpus scan when a type-index folder exists for it, with STUB-MUST-FAIL: plant a corpus-scan resolution for an indexed type -> assert RED. Catches the missing-index/wrong-shape class by construction, not by the next incident.

Boot is READ-MOSTLY: bootstrapSeed does NOT write per Feature on the boot path — seed-if-absent LAZILY at point-of-use (auth path already loads allowedUsers), OR a read-only ASSERT + explicit repair. (Real residual, survives the correction.)
Feature persistence uses an ATOMIC write (temp+rename): a concurrent boot never tears / lost-updates the Feature file (same class as the token-reembed trap).

AUDIT — is `feature` the only type missing an index? MEASURED (2026-08-17): NO. 18 type folders exist; 11 ior:class types IN USE lack one: **Feature** (confirmed genuine, boot-used) + Company, Config, Email, Gate, ModelElement, Phone, Profile, Relationship, TestCase, WebItem. Each must be CLASSIFIED genuine-lost-index vs intentionally-excluded (runtime-PII types Company/Email/Phone/Profile/WebItem may be intentional; Config/Gate/ModelElement/Relationship/TestCase may be sub-types/newer) — architect/PO triage. 'If we lost one we may have lost more' = confirmed.

supersededACs.text: Boot work is INDEPENDENT of corpus size — O(1) or O(features), NEVER O(all-units). DELETE the bootstrapSeed idx.get-every-unit scan; /api/config must answer without scanning the corpus. Provable: boot get-call-count does NOT grow with total-unit-count.

PREFERRED shape: seed-if-absent LAZILY at point-of-use (the auth path already loads allowedUsers) so boot does ZERO corpus work. ACCEPTABLE alternatives: (a) boot as a read-only ASSERT with an EXPLICIT repair path (no silent mutation at boot); (b) FALLBACK — O(features)-via-type-index + ONE ATOMIC write (temp+rename) + a YIELDING loop. NEVER the synchronous zero-yield O(all-units) loop.

A GATE FAILS if boot touches every unit: instrument the ScenarioIndex.get-call-count AND a boot completion-time BUDGET; STUB-MUST-FAIL — plant a corpus scan at boot and assert the gate goes RED. A boot that re-grows to O(corpus) is caught by construction, not by the next outage.

Close the NON-ATOMIC whole-file read-modify-write on Feature writes: a concurrent boot can tear / lost-update the Feature file (same class as the token-reembed trap). Feature persistence uses an atomic write (temp+rename) so a concurrent reader never sees a torn file and no update is lost.

premiseCorrection.correction1_not-slow: The 'O(all-units) scan makes boot slow / degrades daily / latent outage' mechanism was REFUTED by measurement (expert): boot serves ~1.3s, full 5680-unit scan 0.1s; the 45s 'hang' was a broken TLS probe (node fetch rejects self-signed certs); the 8-min outage was the OLD TypeError crash (fixed). Speed was never the point.
premiseCorrection.correction2_structural: Tron RE-FRAMED (the real defect): scenario/sprints.md/ holds a TYPE-INDEX LINK FOLDER for 18 types (bug/changerequest/class/currentsprint/device/file/implementation/message/method/requirement/room/skill/sprint/task/test/tracelink/usecase/user) but **feature is MISSING** — so bootstrapSeed walks all ~5677 units because Features have no index to resolve through. This is a STRUCTURAL regression (a missing type-index), NOT a performance one. RESTORE priority.
